Decision 12

A site scaffolded before this pass, whose setup stopped before its migrations ran, and then resumed with the new create-cairn-site, gets an APP_DB that the deploy provisions and never migrates, so its Signups route reads a database with no table. Only a setup interrupted across this one release reaches the case. The remedy, in the CHANGELOG.md entry: from the affected site, npx wrangler d1 migrations apply APP_DB --remote.

    @@ -11,6 +11,13 @@ this page carries; read `CHANGELOG.md` directly for anything older.
    1111
    1212## Unreleased
    1313
    14+- **Move `editor.nav.configPath` to `editor.siteConfigPath`.** The nav editor, Settings, and Tags all read the one site-config file the adapter names, which defaults to `src/theme/site.config.yaml`. Set the member when your file lives elsewhere. A site that builds a `CairnRuntime` by hand adds `siteConfigPath` to it.
    15+- **Remove `itemLabel` from any `behavior` table, rename any concept whose id names an engine view, and make publish-action labels unique.** `itemLabel` stays on the `array` field descriptor. Composition now throws on a concept id of `login`, `auth`, `editors`, `help`, `media`, `vocabulary`, `nav`, or `settings`, and on two publish actions that share a label.
    16+- **Return a `tagNames` array from every `sanitizeSchema` callback.** The callback now gets a copy of the safe schema, and the engine strips `script` after it returns, so a callback can no longer admit author script. Use a registered component or island for that markup, or `unsafeDisableSanitize` to turn the floor off.
    17+- **Delete your own `devBuildDefine` plugin and `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__` declaration.** The `cairnManifest()` plugin defines the flag now and `/ambient` declares it. A site that keeps both still builds, because a define the site sets wins.
    18+- **Add `@glw907/cairn-cms-dev` to `ssr.noExternal` in `vite.config.ts`.** The package ships built JavaScript that imports `cloudflare:workers`. Without the entry, `vite dev` hands it to Node, which rejects the scheme, and `/admin` answers 500.
    19+- **Drop `seedContent` from `devBackendHandle`, and pass `content: 'fixtures'` when the dev backend runs under `wrangler dev`.** The option never did anything, and the dev backend now serves your site's own content from the working tree by default. That mode needs a filesystem, so it throws under workerd.
    20+- **Pass `content: 'fixtures'` to keep the seeded dev content.** A site that runs the dev backend without ever naming `seedContent` now sees its own entries instead of the sample posts. Edits stay in memory either way, and the admin says so in one persistent notice.
    1421- **Upgrade to SvelteKit 3, `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare` 8, Svelte 5.57.1, and Wrangler 4.118.**
    1522 The engine's peer ranges become `@sveltejs/kit` `^3` and `svelte` `^5.57.1`, and a SvelteKit 2 site
    1623 can't run it. The site also needs Vite `^8.0.12`, `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte` `^7`, and Node

    149+## When your range crosses the scaffold and dev-backend change
    150+
    151+The window that moves the site-config path, tightens composition, and changes the dev backend asks for
    152+these steps, in order, after step 3:
    153+
    154+1. Delete `configPath` from `editor.nav`. If your site config does not live at
    155+ `src/theme/site.config.yaml`, set `editor.siteConfigPath` to its path. A site that builds a
    156+ `CairnRuntime` by hand adds `siteConfigPath` to it.
    157+2. Remove `itemLabel` from any `behavior` table and set it on the `array` field descriptor. Rename a
    158+ concept whose id is `login`, `auth`, `editors`, `help`, `media`, `vocabulary`, `nav`, or `settings`.
    159+ Give every `publishActions` entry a distinct `label`.
    160+3. Make every `sanitizeSchema` callback return a schema with a `tagNames` array. Move any markup that
    161+ needed `<script>` into a registered component or an island.
    162+4. Delete your own `devBuildDefine` plugin and the `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__` declaration in `app.d.ts`.
    163+ The `cairnManifest()` plugin defines the flag, and `@glw907/cairn-cms/ambient` declares it.
    164+5. Add `@glw907/cairn-cms-dev` to `ssr.noExternal` in `vite.config.ts`, beside the engine.
    165+6. Drop `seedContent` from `devBackendHandle`. Pass `content: 'fixtures'` when the dev backend runs
    166+ under `wrangler dev`, or to keep the seeded dev content.
    167+7. Run `npm run check`, then `npm run build`, and expect both to exit 0.
    168+
    169+[Migration notes](./migration-notes.md) carries each item with its reason.
    170+

    7373### Repo tooling

    75+- **`contributor`.** `packages/create-cairn-site/test/fixtures/transcripts/01c-resume.txt` and `01d-resume.txt` still show the two-database provisioning lines, and `01-create-cairn-site.txt` (line 9) still prints the old two-database cost preamble; the scaffold prints neither. They are recorded captures, so only a live re-capture changes them (found by the engine pass B session, 2026-10-10).
    76+- **`contributor`.** `ci-green` run as a background task and piped through `tail` reports the pipe's exit code in the task notification, so a red head reads as exit 0 and the session can take it for green. Engine pass B took six red pushes for green this way (`create-site`, `test`, and `tool` were red). Reading the run list for the head SHA is the check, and a redirect to a file in place of the pipe keeps `ci-green`'s own exit code. The pass-core and cairn-pass skills could say so where they name the watch (found by the engine pass B session, 2026-10-11).
    7577- **`contributor`.** A plan that fixes a task's gate string bypasses the classifier, and the fixed string can omit the type check. The gate economy pass's Task 4a ran a plan-fixed light gate with no `npm run check`, so four `svelte-check` implicit-any errors in `scripts/ci/retries-notice.mjs` reached CI (the test job went red on `d2c5164d`, 2026-10-10) and were fixed under Task 3 (`8695229d`). The classifier would have added `check` for a scripts diff. Found by the gate economy pass conductor, 2026-10-10.
    7678- **`contributor`.** The HISTORY "What the gates caught" bullets name no failing step, so a replay cannot tell which gate leg would have caught a red from the entry alone. The replay's miss-rate floor of 24 items carried failure descriptions that disagreed with the CI logs on 5 of 24 items (it named a missing-package error where the logs show `check:self-use`, `format:check`, and `check:template` findings), and each row had to be re-read from `gh run view --log-failed`. A one-line `failing step` field per caught red would make the next replay a read of HISTORY. Found by the gate economy pass conductor, 2026-10-10.
    7779- **`contributor`.** `cairn-run-gate` records one duration per run and prints no per-leg timing, so the replay's per-leg tables (`docs/superpowers/research/2026-10-09-gate-economy-replay.md`, part 2) mix printed figures (`check:close`, Vitest, Playwright) with legs derived by subtraction. A per-leg line in the run record (or `time` output between `&&` legs) would make the next measurement a read. Found by the gate economy pass conductor, 2026-10-10.

    4647## Tiers and exit codes
    4748
    4849Every finding carries a tier. An error-tier finding gates: it exits the command nonzero, and only a
    49−suppression takes it out of that count. An advisory-tier finding reports and can never change the
    50−exit code, because each advisory rule measures a compositional question a legitimately novel
    51−component can answer differently on purpose.
    50+suppression takes it out of that count. An advisory-tier finding reports and, on a bare call, never
    51+changes the exit code, because each advisory rule measures a compositional question a legitimately
    52+novel component can answer differently on purpose. A pipeline that wants advisories to fail the
    53+build passes `--fail-on advisory`, which exits nonzero on any unsuppressed finding of either tier.
    54+`--fail-on error` states the default. Any other value is a usage error and exits 2.

    5356| Code | What happened |
    5457|---|---|

    58+| 0 | No unsuppressed finding at the gating tier survived |

    21+## The sanitize floor
    22+
    23+Stability tier: Extension API.
    24+
    25+`createRenderer`'s `sanitizeSchema` callback receives a fresh copy of cairn's default schema, so a
    26+change to that copy never reaches another renderer. After the callback returns, cairn removes
    27+`script` from `tagNames` and merges the default `strip` list into the callback's own `strip`
    28+entries. The floor a callback can't lower is exactly that: no `<script>` element survives, and
    29+neither does the body text of any element on the default `strip` list, which holds `script`.
    30+Attributes and URL protocols are the callback's
    31+responsibility, so a callback that admits an unsafe attribute or protocol keeps it.
    32+
    33+`createRenderer` throws when the callback returns no `tagNames` array, because an absent allowlist
    34+admits every element. To turn the floor off, set `unsafeDisableSanitize` instead.
    35+

    2338Stability tier: Extension API.

    85+## Conventions every task follows
    86+
    87+- **Task fields.** Each task gives its outcome, files, risk class, acceptance check, test, and clock
    88+ estimate in minutes. A task is done only when its acceptance passes.
    89+- **Commits.** One commit per task, its subject starting with the task id (`PB-T3: Add the admin
    90+ error page and three scaffold fixes`). Use imperative mood, commit specific files only, and never
    91+ `git add -A`. The body ends with the trailer `Pass-Clock: task=<id> start=<epoch> end=<epoch>
    92+ estimate=<min> fixes=<n>`, read from the clock file before the file is removed.
    93+- **Evidence.** Each quoted proof an old Acceptance asks for (a red run, a mutation and its revert,
    94+ an exit line, a bake or build result) goes in the task commit's message body, trimmed to the lines
    95+ that show the result. A capture is a file under `$HOME/.cache/engine-pre-2b-b/captures/`, named in
    96+ the body. `diff-reviewer` reads the body with the diff, and the PR body links each commit.
    97+- **Proofs on a clean tree.** A revert-based fail-proof or a mutation proof runs only after the
    98+ task's commit, on a clean tree: mutate, or revert a source change with `git checkout <rev> --
    99+ <file>`; quote the red; `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`; confirm `git diff --quiet`; then `git commit
    100+ --amend` the message to add the evidence, before the push. Reason: restoring a file with `git
    101+ checkout` overwrites any uncommitted edit in it. A red-first test on an `auth-data` task quotes the
    102+ red run it got before the code existed.
    103+- **"Fails today" on an `ordinary` task** names why the test is not vacuous; showing the red run is
    104+ optional. The test must still fail with the change reverted, and the close review checks that.
    105+- **Base.** `<base>` is `HEAD` at the task's start, written as a fourth line `base=<sha>` in the clock
    106+ file (the clock hook reads only `task=`, `start=`, and `estimate=`). Two exceptions: PB-T1's base is
    107+ PB-T0's first parent (`git rev-parse <PB-T0 sha>^1`), so the range carries the WIP; a pair merge's
    108+ base is the commit the pair was dispatched from.

    110+ <base>..HEAD` prints the legs, and each leg runs through `cairn-run-gate` per `cairn-pass`. The
    111+ fast lane runs no `create-cairn-site` suite, no `integration` project, no `packages/cairn-cms-dev`
    112+ test, and no e2e (`docs/internal/pass-gate-tiers.md`, "The fast lane"), so a task whose tests live
    113+ there names them under Extra commands, run beside the lane. Every task whose range touches
    114+ `packages/create-cairn-site/**`, `examples/showcase/**`, `templates/waymark/**`, or

    116+ read the bake, which emits from the showcase. A task acceptance that quotes its own
    117+ command (a fresh bake, a `wrangler deploy --dry-run` replay, a `node -e` one-liner) also runs beside
    118+ the lane. No task waits for CI before the next. A red stops the line, and the fix goes forward or

    125+ - The integration project, heavy: `cairn-run-gate 'npm run test:integration'`

    127+ port guard comes first because `playwright.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`,

    130+- **CI reads.** `ci-green` exit 1 is a red. Exit 2 is a red unless one re-push clears it. Exit 3 is

    177+ resume: claude attach engine-pass-b"` (Geoff, 2026-10-10: "Normal urgency"); and ends its turn.
    178+ Every wake-up tick first runs `test -e "$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/pass-stop"`, and a
    179+ relaunch runs Resume step 2. While the file exists, the turn ends with no other act. The session
    180+ removes the file only in a turn that answers a message from Geoff saying to go on, and that turn's
    181+ first tool call is one Bash call that removes the file and rewrites the clock: `g=$(git rev-parse
    182+ --absolute-git-dir) && rm "$g/pass-stop" && { test ! -f "$g/pass-task-clock" || sed -i
    183+ "s/^start=.*/start=$(date +%s)/" "$g/pass-task-clock"; }` (or `estimate=` to Geoff's figure). A
    184+ clock-stop line that arrives before that call, or in the same turn as it, is stale and is not a
    185+ stop: the hook fires after every tool call and reads the old `start=`. The wait between a stop's
    186+ notification and Geoff's reply is excluded from the success-test clock (planner's ruling: a pause
    187+ under ruling 13 and the spec's exclusion of "pauses he orders"), and the score reports it as its own
    188+ line. A resumed
    189+ `auth-data` task never re-dispatches `diff-reviewer` on an unchanged commit to overturn a standing
    190+ verdict. These stop the line:
    191+ - A fired clock stop.
    192+ - A red the session cannot fix in two attempts, a `ci-green` exit 2 that a re-push does not clear,
    193+ or a red local full gate on a PB-C exit 3.
    194+ - An `auth-data` `fix` that still stands after one fix round, or an `escalate`.
    195+ - A task needing public surface the old plan does not name (old Global constraints, "No new public
    196+ surface"), or a finding that would change the approved design.
    197+ - A pair's sleep exiting before both agents return (above), or a merge conflict, except a STATUS
    198+ conflict under "Merging `main`".
    199+ - At PB-C, a blocking finding the session would overrule (item 3), or a third merge-in of `main`.
    200+ - On battery with no mains supply online, at 11 percent: commit the work in progress, then stop
    201+ (`unattended-work-guards.md`, "Battery floor").
    202+- **Merging `main`.** A merge of `origin/main` into the pass branch resolves a `docs/STATUS.md`
    203+ conflict by hand, keeping both sides' lines. Any other conflict is a stop.
    204+- **Pushes.** Push the session's own branch to `glw907/cairn-cms` after every task, then start
    205+ `ci-green <sha> --pr <n> --wait` as a background Bash task, re-issued on 75. Never push `main`. The
    206+ only merge into `main` is PB-C's.
    207+- **Resume.** A relaunch runs the launch prompt again, which does these in order:
    208+ 1. If `/var/home/glw907/Projects/cairn-cms/.claude/worktrees/engine-pass-b` appears in `git worktree
    209+ list`, call EnterWorktree with that `path`. Otherwise call it with `name: engine-pass-b`, which
    210+ creates the worktree on branch `worktree-engine-pass-b`.
    211+ 2. One Bash call, the first after EnterWorktree, checks the stop and resets the clock: `g=$(git
    212+ rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); if test -e "$g/pass-stop"; then cat "$g/pass-stop"; elif test
    213+ -f "$g/pass-task-clock"; then sed -i "s/^start=.*/start=$(date +%s)/" "$g/pass-task-clock"; fi`.
    214+ If it prints the stop, end the turn. A clock-stop line that arrives before this call, or in the
    215+ same turn as it, is stale and is not a stop.
    216+ 3. `gh pr list --head worktree-engine-pass-b --state all` finds the PR; never open a second one. If
    217+ it shows `MERGED`, run only PB-C item 8.
    218+ 4. If `git status --porcelain` prints anything, run `git stash push -u -m resume-<task>`, never a
    219+ discard, then judge the stash against the in-flight task's acceptance: re-apply it, or leave it
    220+ stashed and name it in the PR body.
    221+ 5. `git branch --list 'worktree-agent-*'`: merge any branch whose commits carry a pair task id
    222+ before re-dispatching that task.
    223+ 6. Find the done tasks with `git log --oneline` (task ids in subjects; skip subjects that start
    224+ with `Record a stop`), and start at the first task whose acceptance fails. If its clock file was
    225+ not reset in step 2, write it fresh. Inside PB-C, start at the first item whose PR body section
    226+ is missing.
    227+
    228+ A live session that is waiting resumes with `claude attach engine-pass-b`. A dead one is relaunched
    229+ with the Launch block, which runs its checks again.
    230+- **PR body.** Fixed `##` sections, in this order: `What landed` (task id, commit), `auth-data
    231+ verdicts`, `Consumer proof`, `Review`, `Visual`, `Smoke`, `Retried tests` (every one from
    232+ `ci-green`'s output), `Found, not done`, `Decision 12`, and `Score`. The session keeps the draft at

    588+```bash
    589+(
    590+cd /var/home/glw907/Projects/cairn-cms && git fetch origin &&
    591+out=$(claude agents --json) && jq -e 'type == "array"' <<<"$out" >/dev/null &&
    592+! jq -e 'any(.[]; .name == "engine-pass-b" or ((.cwd // "") | test("/[.]claude/worktrees/(engine-pass-b|engine-pre-2b-b)($|/)")))' <<<"$out" >/dev/null &&

    594+[ "$(git branch --show-current)" = main ] &&
    595+git merge --ff-only origin/main &&
    596+[ "$(git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD)" = 0 ] &&
    597+P=.claude/worktrees/engine-pre-2b-b &&
    598+[ -z "$(git -C "$P" status --porcelain)" ] &&
    599+[ "$(git rev-parse engine-pre-2b-b)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/engine-pre-2b-b)" ] &&
    600+git check-ignore -q .claude/worktrees/x &&
    601+claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium --name engine-pass-b \
    602+ "$(cat "$P/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-engine-pass-b-lean-prompt.txt")"
    603+) || echo "launch refused: a check failed" >&2
    604+```

    606+The `claude agents --json` lines fail closed: a failed listing or a non-array refuses the launch, and

    608+`origin/main..HEAD` count catches unpushed commits on local `main`, since `worktree.baseRef: "head"`
    609+branches from local `HEAD`. The last two checks before `claude --bg` make the plan the session reads
    610+equal to the pushed branch tip PB-T0 merges.

    153+### V1 (major). A relaunch or a "go on" turn fires a stale clock stop before Resume rewrites `start=`
    154+
    155+- **Location.** Plan `:189-203` (`start=` is rewritten at step 6), `:167-172`, `:173`; prompt `:6-8`.
    156+- **Defect.** `claude-clock-stop` is a PostToolUse hook, and it fires after every tool call once the
    157+ cwd is the pass worktree. After a crash, the leftover `pass-task-clock` usually sits past twice its
    158+ estimate. EnterWorktree's own call, the stop check, `gh pr list`, `git status`, and `git branch`
    159+ each return "Clock stop: ... Write STATUS, run `notify-send -u normal`, and wait for Geoff" before
    160+ step 6 rewrites `start=`. Stops lists "A fired clock stop", so a faithful executor writes
    161+ `pass-stop` and ends, which turns every crash relaunch into an attended stop. The "go on" turn has
    162+ the same hazard: its first tool call, before it rewrites `start=`, gets the stale stop line.
    163+ Integrity M3's "Stale clock" item is therefore not closed.
    164+- **Evidence.** `claude-clock-stop:13-27`, `~/.claude/settings.json:111-115`; `pass-core` "A resume
    165+ rewrites `start=`".
    166+- **Fix.** Make the stop check and the clock reset one Bash call, the first after EnterWorktree, in
    167+ both the prompt and Resume step 2:
    168+ `g=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir); if test -e "$g/pass-stop"; then cat "$g/pass-stop"; elif test -f "$g/pass-task-clock"; then sed -i "s/^start=.*/start=$(date +%s)/" "$g/pass-task-clock"; fi`.
    169+ Add one sentence: "A clock-stop line that arrives before this call, or in the same turn as it, is
    170+ stale and is not a stop." The "go on" turn removes `pass-stop` and rewrites `start=` (or
    171+ `estimate=`) in one call. Drop the rewrite from step 6.

    177+ red local gate as a stop. Merge step 5 requires exit 0 and stops at the first failure. An executor
    178+ can resolve this by merging after a local gate, with no CI read of the final head.
    179+- **Fix.** Merge step 5: "exits 0. Exit 3 here is a stop: no self-merge without CI on the head."
    180+ Scope the "CI reads" sentence to the fix chain.

    186+ 7, and the merge then joins a pair of heads that no one tested together. Integrity M1 named "too

    189+ rev-parse origin/main)" ]`, and on a failure return to step 3.

    274+Not launch-ready yet, and one major blocks it. V1 turns the first crash relaunch, and every "go on"

    279+Once V1 and the minors are folded, Geoff has ruled on both rulings (V8), and this file is committed

    1+# Engine pass B lean re-plan: contract and criteria review
    2+
    3+Lens: contract and criteria. Target: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-engine-pass-b-lean.md`
    4+(called "lean" below) and its launch prompt, at `18cd15db`, binding sections of
    5+`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-engine-pass-pre-2b-b.md` (called "old" below). Probed against
    6+`origin/main` `dea73f7d`, `origin/worktree-lean-cutover` (PR #112, `scripts/checks/gate-tier.mjs`,
    7+`docs/internal/pass-gate-tiers.md`), `pass-core`, `cairn-pass`, the agent definitions
    8+(`cairn-implementer`, `diff-reviewer`), the `claude-clock-stop` hook, and the `EnterWorktree` tool
    9+contract. Read-only; nothing was run beyond `git show`, `git log`, `grep`, and `gh pr view`.
    10+
    11+Counts: 1 blocker, 13 major, 20 minor. Three findings are over-ceremony: 14 (major), 32, and 33.
    12+No owner fork: every resolution below is a method call.
    13+
    14+## Key fact the plan is missing
    15+
    16+The fast lane is narrower than the old "computed gate" in ways that matter for this plan's
    17+acceptance lines. In `decideFastGate` (`gate-tier.mjs` on PR #112, roughly `:644-713`) and in
    18+`pass-gate-tiers.md` "The fast lane" (`:113-138`):
    19+
    20+- The unit leg is `npx vitest related --run --passWithNoTests --project unit <paths>`, and only
    21+ paths matching `/^(?:src|scripts)\//` are inputs. A changed `packages/cairn-cms-dev/src/*.ts`
    22+ is never an input, though its tests sit in the `unit` project (`vitest.config.ts`, the `unit`
    23+ include list).
    24+- It never runs `npm test -w packages/create-cairn-site` (`CREATE_CAIRN_SITE` appears only in the
    25+ targeted gate, `:599`), the `integration` project, the whole node projects, or any e2e spec
    26+ ("It runs no whole node project and no e2e").
    27+
    28+So "An old 'the computed gate green' line now means the fast lane green" (lean `:62-63`) silently
    29+drops the local run of PB-T1's three test-first tests, PB-T10's overlay and guard tests, PB-T9's
    30+integration cases, and PB-T3's A5 e2e spec. CI still carries them, so nothing is lost at merge, but
    31+several acceptance lines cannot be met or evidenced as written. Findings 3 and 4 fold this.
    32+
    33+## Findings, ranked by consequence
    34+
    35+### 1. Blocker: PB-C's acceptance lets the session merge with a blocking finding open
    36+
    37+- **Location:** lean `:270-271`, `:292-295`; also `:39-41`.
    38+- **Defect:** The acceptance reads "the review's verdict is `accept`, or each finding is
    39+ dispositioned in the PR body". A blocking security finding written off as "won't fix" in the PR
    40+ body passes this, and the merge in item 9 then follows unattended. `pass-core` "Close" requires
    41+ more: "An overruled verdict is stated with its reason in the PR body, and a correctness-critical
    42+ overrule re-runs the review at `xhigh`." The plan carries no `xhigh` re-run and no stop. On an
    43+ `auth-data` pass that merges itself, this is the one gate between an open blocker and `main`.
    44+ The acceptance also omits half of PB-C's own outcome: the consumer proof's evidence (item 2), the
    45+ `visual-verifier` verdict (item 3), ROADMAP's entry removal, the `CHANGELOG.md` finalization, and
    46+ the score.
    47+- **Fold:** Replace the clause with: "the whole-branch review returns `accept`, or every BLOCKING
    48+ finding is fixed in the fix chain; a NON-BLOCKING finding may be dispositioned in the PR body. An
    49+ overrule of a BLOCKING finding re-runs the review at `xhigh` (`pass-core`), and a BLOCKING finding
    50+ that still stands after that, or any overrule on an `auth-data` path, is a stop under 'Stops' and
    51+ blocks the merge. `visual-verifier` returns no STRUCTURAL verdict, or each is fixed." Add
    52+ acceptance items for the consumer proof's three quoted exit lines, `git diff origin/main --
    53+ ROADMAP.md` showing the entry removed, and the PR body carrying the six score rows.
    54+
    55+### 2. Major: no home for per-task evidence ("the report")
    56+

    36+### B1 (blocker). A stop is not durable, and nothing mechanical blocks the merge on an open stop
    37+
    38+- **Location.** `lean:79-84` (Stops), `lean:39-41` (an open stop blocks the merge), `lean:286-295`
    39+ (item 9 and the acceptance), `prompt:8-9` (arm the API-drop wake-up).

    41+ ends its turn. The prompt also arms the `/loop` fallback wake-up. Per
    42+ `unattended-work-guards.md`, each tick "resumes at the first task whose acceptance fails". A
    43+ deliberate stop looks exactly like a halted run. The next tick resumes:
    44+ - After a review `escalate` or a standing `fix`, the resume re-runs the task's acceptance,
    45+ including "`diff-reviewer` returns `accept`". That re-rolls the reviewer until it accepts.
    46+ - After a red the session could not fix in two attempts, it tries a third time.
    47+
    48+ The clock stop re-fires through its hook only while the clock file stays. No other stop leaves a
    49+ machine-readable mark. "An open stop blocks the merge" has no check anywhere, and the PB-C
    50+ acceptance has no line for it. An unattended executor can therefore get past its own auth-data
    51+ stop and merge.

    61+ commit to overturn a standing verdict.

    87+- **Location.** `lean:260-262`, `lean:286-288`, `lean:292-295`.
    88+- **Defect.** With no branch protection, the session's checks are the only gate, and they have

    12+### B1. The WIP is merged in PB-T0, so PB-T1's single commit, fast lane, and task review cannot cover old Task 2 (blocker)
    13+
    14+- **Location.** Plan `:113-115` (PB-T0 merges `engine-pre-2b-b`, bringing WIP `dbdc4556`),
    15+ `:136-141` (PB-T1 "landing as one commit", "Start from WIP `dbdc4556`"), `:59-60` (fast lane
    16+ `--range <base>..HEAD`, `<base>` never defined), and `:65-66` ("`diff-reviewer` ... reads the
    17+ commit").
    18+- **Defect.** PB-T0's merge makes `dbdc4556` an existing commit on the pass branch. PB-T1's commit
    19+ then holds only the session's delta on top of the WIP. It cannot hold "old Tasks 1 and 2 as one
    20+ commit" unless the session squashes. Two consequences follow:
    21+ - If `<base>` is the commit before the task, the natural reading, then `<base>..HEAD` leaves out
    22+ the WIP's 35 files, and the fast lane never gates them.
    23+ - `diff-reviewer` "reads the commit", so it never reads most of old Task 2's `auth-data` change.
    24+
    25+ The spec requires both: "Its WIP for Tasks 1 and 2 ... is re-gated through the fast lane; Task 2
    26+ gets the `auth-data` read" (lean spec, Rollout step 5).
    27+- **Evidence.** `git diff --name-only 21ec86a9 engine-pre-2b-b` lists 35 WIP paths, among them
    28+ `packages/create-cairn-site/src/cloudflare/{deploy,chapter,config}.mjs`,
    29+ `examples/showcase/wrangler.jsonc`, and `templates/waymark/src/routes/admin/signups/*`. That set
    30+ is `auth-data` by `cairn-pass`'s path map (`packages/create-cairn-site/src/{github,cloudflare}/**`,
    31+ `wrangler.*`, `**/admin/signups/**`). gate-tier's `diffEntries(range)` sees only the range's paths
    32+ (`gate-tier.mjs` main, step 2 branch). `cairn-pass` and `cairn-implementer.md` also leave
    33+ `<base>` undefined.
    34+- **Fold.**
    35+ 1. Define `<base>` once in Conventions: the commit before the task starts, recorded as a fourth
    36+ line `base=<sha>` in the clock file. The hook reads only the first three keys, so a fourth
    37+ line is safe. For a pair, the base is the commit before dispatch.

    43+ that keeps `dbdc4556` out of the history (squash is the worse choice, since PB-T0 already

    198+ never fires. The pass B branch does not touch STATUS. It can stay as a guard.

    200+### m5. A hung pair never trips the clock stop (minor)
    201+
    202+- **Location.** Plan `:75-78`.
    203+- **Defect.** This matches `pass-core` ("Pair worktrees hold no clock file, so the stop cannot fire
    204+ while the session waits on a pair"), but nothing wakes the session if a pair agent stalls. The
    205+ hook runs only after the session's own tool calls, and while it waits it makes none.
    206+- **Evidence.** `claude-clock-stop` resolves `git -C "$cwd" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` from the
    207+ hook input's `cwd`, and prints nothing when the file is absent.
    208+- **Fold.** At dispatch, start a background Bash `sleep $((2*<longer estimate>*60))`. Its exit
    209+ re-invokes the session, which then checks the pair and treats an unreturned pair as a fired
    210+ stop.
    211+
    212+### m6. The clock hook goes blind while the session's cwd sits in a scratch clone (minor)
    213+

    215+ `$HOME/.cache/engine-pre-2b-b/`. A clone is its own git repo, so a persistent `cd` there makes the
    216+ hook read that clone's git dir. It finds no file and stays silent.
    217+- **Fold.** Run scratch work in a subshell or with `-C`/`--prefix`, and keep the session's cwd at
    218+ the worktree root.
    219+
    220+### m7. The marker replays write under `/tmp`, and their line numbers moved (minor)
    221+

    224+ in every shard leg, the default build at `:79-97` with `--outdir=/tmp/dev-fold-default` and the
    225+ flagged build at `:132-146`, up from `:68`/`:121` on `main`. `scaffold.yml` is unchanged
    226+ (`:45-61`, `:62-76`). A verbatim replay writes `/tmp`, which the old Global constraints forbid
    227+ ("never `/tmp`").
    228+- **Fold.** Replay with `--outdir="$HOME/.cache/engine-pre-2b-b/dev-fold-{default,flagged}"`, and
    229+ record the step-2 line numbers in PB-T0's amendment.
    230+
    231+### m8. `ci-green` does not check the run's base, and `main` can move before the merge (minor)
    232+
    233+- **Location.** Plan `:260-261`, `:286-287`, `:292`.
    234+- **Evidence.** `ci-green-lib.mjs:434` uses `merge-base origin/main <sha>` only to size the
    235+ expected set. Nothing checks that the PR run tested the current `main`. The repo allows merge
    236+ commits (`allow_merge_commit: true`), and `main` is unprotected (branch protection returns 404),
    237+ so `gh pr merge <n> --merge` succeeds even when `main` moved after the CI read.
    238+- **Fold.** Make the base check a command: `git fetch origin && git merge-base --is-ancestor
    239+ origin/main HEAD`. Run it at item 1 and again immediately before `gh pr merge`. On a failure,
    240+ merge `main`, push, and read CI again. `gh pr close 111 --comment` and `gh pr merge --merge` were
    241+ confirmed in `gh` help.

    243+### m9. The score under-counts pair gate time and mislabels the off-path CI time (minor)

    245+- **Location.** Plan `:281-285`.

    247+ `toplevel` and `branch` match. Pair agents gate in `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` on
    248+ `worktree-agent-*` branches, and the session waits on them. It sums concurrent legs and every CI
    249+ wait, most of which run off the path in the background.

    251+ critical path". Label the CI sum as total, and count only the CI waits that blocked a task as on
    252+ the path.

    259+ commit, which confirms `baseRef: head` forks pair agents from the session worktree's HEAD.

    261+ branches, after the m9 records read.

    2+// injected pieces, so a unit test drives it without the theme's Svelte imports. feed.ts binds it
    3+// to this site.
    4+import type { CairnAdapter } from '@glw907/cairn-cms';
    5+import {
    6+ createFragmentResolver,
    7+ createLinkResolver,
    8+ type FeedItem,
    9+ type MediaResolve,
    10+ type SiteResolver,
    11+} from '@glw907/cairn-cms/delivery';
    12+
    13+/** What the feed reads: the site, its origin, the render call, and the media resolver. */
    14+export interface FeedSource {
    15+ site: SiteResolver;
    16+ origin: string;
    17+ render: CairnAdapter['rendering']['render'];
    18+ resolveMedia: MediaResolve;
    19+}
    20+
    21+/**
    22+ * Map a site's posts into feed items. A feed body leaves the site, so each link and each image
    23+ * URL is absolute, and `::include` fragments render from the site's own fragments.
    24+ */
    25+export async function feedItemsFrom({
    26+ site,
    27+ origin,
    28+ render,
    29+ resolveMedia,
    30+}: FeedSource): Promise<FeedItem[]> {
    31+ const posts = site.concept('posts');
    32+ if (!posts) return [];
    33+ const toPermalink = createLinkResolver(site);
    34+ const resolve = (ref: Parameters<typeof toPermalink>[0]) => origin + toPermalink(ref);
    35+ const resolveFragment = createFragmentResolver(site);
    36+ const resolveAbsoluteMedia: MediaResolve = (ref) => {
    37+ const url = resolveMedia(ref);
    38+ return url === undefined ? undefined : new URL(url, origin).href;
    39+ };
    40+ return Promise.all(
    41+ posts.all().map(async (p) => ({
    42+ title: p.title,
    43+ url: origin + p.permalink,
    44+ date: p.date,
    45+ summary: p.excerpt,
    46+ contentHtml: await render({
    47+ body: posts.byId(p.id)!.body,
    48+ resolve,
    49+ resolveMedia: resolveAbsoluteMedia,
    50+ resolveFragment,
    51+ }),
    52+ tags: p.tags,
    53+ })),
    54+ );
    55+}

    52+## Choose the content
    53+
    54+`devBackendHandle` takes a `content` option that picks what the dev admin serves.
    55+
    56+| `content` | What the admin serves |
    57+| --- | --- |
    58+| `'repository'` (the default) | Your site's own files. Each branch is an in-memory overlay over the working tree. |
    59+| `'fixtures'` | The package's seeded in-memory repo: sample posts, media, fragments, and a tag vocabulary. |
    60+
    61+In `'repository'` mode a read answers the overlay first and the disk second, so the admin lists the
    62+entries in your `src/content`, your manifest, your site config, and your media record. A save,
    63+delete, rename, publish, Settings save, nav save, or media upload writes only the overlay, so
    64+nothing reaches disk and a restart drops every edit. The admin says so in one persistent notice:
    65+"Edits are held in memory. They're discarded when the dev server stops." An edit you make to a file
    66+on disk shows on the next request, unless the dev admin has already written that file, in which case
    67+the admin's copy wins until the dev server restarts.
    68+
    69+The limits:
    70+
    71+- The mode reads the filesystem, so it throws under `wrangler dev`, whose workerd has none. Pass
    72+ `content: 'fixtures'` for a `wrangler dev` session, which is also what a site's end-to-end suite
    73+ that asserts seeded content wants.
    74+- Uploaded media bytes land in the in-memory R2 double, not your local R2, so a thumbnail for a file
    75+ you uploaded before the restart is gone after it.
    76+- Paths resolve against `process.cwd()`, so start the dev server from the site's root.
    77+
    6478## The fence
    6579
    6680Three independent layers keep the bypass out of production. The bypass ships only if all three fail.

    2+// in-memory overlay over the site's working tree. A read answers the overlay first and the disk
    3+// second, so the dev admin lists the developer's real entries; a commit writes only the overlay, so

    5+// the seeded in-memory repo this mode replaces for a real site.
    6+import type { Backend, BackendCommit, CommitAuthor, FileChange, RepoFile } from '@glw907/cairn-cms';
    7+import { BranchExistsError, CommitConflictError } from '@glw907/cairn-cms';

    10+type Overlay = Map<string, string | null>;
    11+
    12+/** A commit kept for `listCommits` and for a read at a past commit's sha. */
    13+interface LoggedCommit {

    15+ paths: string[];

    23+const ABSENT = new Set(['ENOENT', 'ENOTDIR', 'EISDIR']);

    25+/**
    26+ * Build the repository-mode `Backend` over the working tree at `root`. The overlay lives in this
    27+ * closure, so one backend is one dev session: construct it once per handle, never per request.
    28+ * `node:fs` loads on first read, the way `channel-db.ts` loads `node:sqlite`, so importing this
    29+ * module costs nothing under a bundler that never reaches a read.
    30+ * @param root - the working-tree directory every repo path resolves against, normally `process.cwd()`.
    31+ * @returns a {@link Backend} marked `ephemeral`, with `main` as its default branch.
    32+ */
    33+export function createRepositoryBackend(root: string): Backend {
    34+ const branches = new Map<string, Overlay>([['main', new Map()]]);
    35+ let seq = 0;
    36+ const nextSha = () => `repo-sha-${++seq}`;
    37+ const heads = new Map<string, string>([['main', nextSha()]]);
    38+ const log: LoggedCommit[] = [];
    39+
    40+ /** Resolve a repo path against the root, refusing one that escapes it. */
    41+ async function onDisk(path: string): Promise<string> {
    42+ const { resolve, sep } = await import('node:path');
    43+ const base = resolve(root);
    44+ const absolute = resolve(base, path);
    45+ if (absolute !== base && !absolute.startsWith(base + sep)) {
    46+ throw new Error(`cairn dev backend: "${path}" resolves outside the working tree`);
    47+ }
    48+ return absolute;
    49+ }
    50+
    51+ async function diskRead(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
    52+ const { readFile } = await import('node:fs/promises');
    53+ try {
    54+ return await readFile(await onDisk(path), 'utf8');
    55+ } catch (error) {
    56+ if (ABSENT.has((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? '')) return null;
    57+ throw error;
    58+ }
    59+ }
    60+
    61+ async function diskNames(dir: string): Promise<string[]> {
    62+ const { readdir } = await import('node:fs/promises');
    63+ try {
    64+ const entries = await readdir(await onDisk(dir), { withFileTypes: true });
    65+ return entries.filter((entry) => entry.isFile()).map((entry) => entry.name);
    66+ } catch (error) {
    67+ if (ABSENT.has((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? '')) return [];
    68+ throw error;
    69+ }
    70+ }
    71+
    72+ return {
    73+ defaultBranch: 'main',
    74+ ephemeral: true,
    75+
    76+ async readFile(path, ref) {
    77+ const overlay = branches.get(ref);
    78+ if (overlay) return overlay.has(path) ? (overlay.get(path) ?? null) : diskRead(path);
    79+ // `ref` may name a recorded commit sha rather than a live branch (a revert's target read).
    80+ const historical = log.find((entry) => entry.ref === ref && entry.paths.includes(path));
    81+ return historical ? (historical.contentByPath[path] ?? null) : null;
    82+ },
    83+
    84+ async readEntries(dir, ref): Promise<RepoFile[]> {
    85+ const overlay = branches.get(ref);
    86+ if (!overlay) return [];
    87+ const clean = dir.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, '');
    88+ const prefix = `${clean}/`;
    89+ const names = new Set((await diskNames(clean)).filter((name) => name.endsWith('.md')));
    90+ for (const [path, content] of overlay) {
    91+ if (!path.startsWith(prefix) || !path.endsWith('.md')) continue;
    92+ const name = path.slice(prefix.length);
    93+ if (name.includes('/')) continue;
    94+ if (content === null) names.delete(name);
    95+ else names.add(name);
    96+ }
    97+ return [...names]
    98+ .map((name) => ({ id: name.replace(/\.md$/, ''), name, path: `${prefix}${name}` }))
    99+ .sort((a, b) => b.id.localeCompare(a.id));
    100+ },
    101+
    102+ async branchHead(branch) {
    103+ return heads.get(branch) ?? null;
    104+ },
    105+
    106+ async listBranches(prefix) {
    107+ return [...branches.keys()].filter((name) => name.startsWith(prefix)).sort();
    108+ },
    109+
    110+ async commit(branch, changes: FileChange[], author, _message, expectedHead) {
    111+ if (changes.length === 0) throw new Error('commitFiles: no changes to commit');
    112+ if (expectedHead !== undefined && heads.get(branch) !== expectedHead) {
    113+ throw new CommitConflictError(`${branch} (head moved)`);
    114+ }
    115+ const overlay = branches.get(branch) ?? new Map<string, string | null>();
    116+ branches.set(branch, overlay);
    117+ const contentByPath: Record<string, string | null> = {};
    118+ for (const change of changes) {
    119+ overlay.set(change.path, change.content);
    120+ contentByPath[change.path] = change.content;
    121+ }
    122+ const sha = nextSha();
    123+ heads.set(branch, sha);
    124+ log.push({
    125+ branch,
    126+ paths: changes.map((change) => change.path),
    127+ ref: sha,
    128+ author,
    129+ date: new Date().toISOString(),
    130+ contentByPath,
    131+ });
    132+ return sha;
    133+ },
    134+
    135+ async listCommits(path, ref, limit): Promise<BackendCommit[]> {
    136+ return log
    137+ .filter((entry) => entry.branch === ref && entry.paths.includes(path))
    138+ .reverse()
    139+ .slice(0, limit + 1)
    140+ .map((entry) => ({ ref: entry.ref, author: entry.author, date: entry.date }));
    141+ },
    142+
    143+ async createBranch(name, fromBranch) {
    144+ if (branches.has(name)) throw new BranchExistsError(name);
    145+ const source = branches.get(fromBranch);
    146+ if (!source) throw new CommitConflictError(`${fromBranch} (unreadable source)`);
    147+ branches.set(name, new Map(source));
    148+ const sha = nextSha();
    149+ heads.set(name, sha);
    150+ return sha;
    151+ },
    152+
    153+ async deleteBranch(name) {
    154+ branches.delete(name);
    155+ heads.delete(name);
    156+ },
    157+ };

    48+/** The backend the handle puts on `locals.cairnBackend` for one admin request. */
    49+async function backendFor(content?: 'repository' | 'fixtures'): Promise<Backend> {
    50+ const handle: Handle = devBackendHandle({ runtime: {}, ...(content ? { content } : {}) });
    51+ const event = { url: new URL('http://localhost/admin'), locals: {} as Record<string, unknown> };
    52+ await handle({ event: event as unknown as Parameters<Handle>[0]['event'], resolve: async () => new Response('ok') });

    56+/** Every file under `dir` with its bytes' hash and mtime, keyed by relative path. */
    57+function snapshot(dir: string, base = dir): Record<string, string> {
    58+ const out: Record<string, string> = {};
    59+ for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    60+ const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    61+ if (entry.isDirectory()) Object.assign(out, snapshot(full, base));
    62+ else {
    63+ const digest = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(full)).digest('hex');
    64+ out[full.slice(base.length + 1)] = `${digest}:${statSync(full).mtimeMs}`;
    65+ }
    66+ }
    67+ return out;

    453+
    454+Its `+page.server.ts`, which reads and writes the developer's own `signups` table through a D1
    455+binding the site declares itself. The access rule it relies on lives in the showcase adapter's
    456+`access` member; a site that copies the screen adds its own rule for the route.
    457+
    458+```ts
    459+// Archetype: the custom admin screen over the site's own table.
    460+// Atoms: requireAccess, createSectionAction, createLogger.
    461+// Recipe: docs/extend/add-a-custom-admin-screen.md.
    462+//
    463+// A developer's own custom admin screen, proving the extension seam. It is a concrete route
    464+// under /admin (so it wins over the catch-all), inherits the guard-populated locals.cairnEditor, renders
    465+// inside the shared CairnAdminShell from the parent layout, and reads and writes its own APP_DB
    466+// binding (the engine never touches it). requireAccess on the load and the section action's own
    467+// access check on each form action resolve against the same site access map, so a denied POST's
    468+// page render exposes nothing the load would already have refused; the ownerOnly nav flag is
    469+// cosmetic only.
    470+import type { PageServerLoad, Actions } from './$types';
    471+import { env } from 'cloudflare:workers';
    472+import { createSectionAction, requireAccess } from '@glw907/cairn-cms/sveltekit';
    473+import { error, fail } from '@sveltejs/kit';
    474+import type { D1Database } from '@cloudflare/workers-types';
    475+import { log } from '#lib/log.js';
    476+
    477+/** A signup row, the developer's own table shape, read from APP_DB. */
    478+interface SignupRow {
    479+ id: number;
    480+ name: string;
    481+ email: string;
    482+}
    483+
    484+// A deployed Worker always carries APP_DB (wrangler.jsonc binds it); its absence is a
    485+// deployment misconfiguration, not a request-shaped failure, so it logs with the engine's own
    486+// area.subject.verb_phrase grammar (section-action.ts's admin.action.misconfigured) and fails
    487+// closed with a generic 500 rather than leaking binding detail to the client. The load resolves
    488+// the binding this way because createSectionAction wraps form actions only; requireAccess and
    489+// requireOwner are the documented gates for a load.
    490+function requireAppDb(): D1Database {
    491+ const db: D1Database | undefined = env.APP_DB;
    492+ if (!db) {
    493+ log.error('admin.signups.misconfigured', { reason: 'db_not_bound' });
    494+ error(500, 'This screen is not configured.');
    495+ }
    496+ return db;
    497+}
    498+
    499+export const load: PageServerLoad = async (event) => {
    500+ requireAccess(event);
    501+ const db = requireAppDb();
    502+ const { results } = await db
    503+ .prepare('SELECT id, name, email FROM signups ORDER BY id DESC')
    504+ .all<SignupRow>();
    505+ return { signups: results };
    506+};
    507+
    508+// This screen's job is to teach the documented path, so it copies the wrapper rather than the
    509+// minimum that compiles: createSectionAction (@glw907/cairn-cms/sveltekit) is what a site's own
    510+// admin section reaches for, and a developer copying this route should carry it across. It
    511+// composes the editor, CSRF and audit contract onto every action and resolves the section's own
    512+// binding, so no action re-implements a gate the engine already owns.
    513+//

    1+// The cairnManifest plugin's `config` hook supplies `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__`, the build-time half of
    2+// the dev-backend gate. The define decides whether a handle that mints owner sessions compiles into
    3+// a deployed Worker, so each case pins one way it could fold the wrong direction: the default build
    4+// must read false, `vite dev` and an explicit VITE_CAIRN_E2E=1 opt-in must read true, and a define
    5+// the site already set must survive whichever plugin order Vite merges the hooks in.
    6+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
    7+import { mkdtempSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
    8+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
    9+import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
    10+import { resolveConfig, type Plugin } from 'vite';
    11+import { cairnManifest } from '../../lib/vite/internal.js';
    12+
    13+const OPTS = {
    14+ configModule: '/src/lib/cairn.config.ts',
    15+ content: { posts: '/src/content/posts/*.md' },
    16+ manifestPath: '/src/content/.cairn/index.json',
    17+};
    18+
    19+const REPO_ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../../..');
    20+
    21+type ConfigHook = (
    22+ config: Record<string, unknown>,
    23+ env: { command: 'build' | 'serve'; mode: string },
    24+) => Promise<{ define?: Record<string, string> } | undefined>;
    25+
    26+/** Run the plugin's `config` hook the way Vite does, returning the define it contributes. */
    27+async function defineFor(command: 'build' | 'serve', mode: string, config: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
    28+ const hook = cairnManifest(OPTS).config as unknown as ConfigHook;
    29+ const result = await hook(config, { command, mode });
    30+ return result?.define?.__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__;
    31+}
    32+
    33+const scratch: string[] = [];
    34+
    35+/** A throwaway app root whose `vite` resolves to the repo's, holding the named env files. */
    36+function appRootWith(envFiles: Record<string, string>): string {
    37+ const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cairn-dev-define-'));
    38+ scratch.push(root);
    39+ mkdirSync(join(root, 'node_modules'));
    40+ symlinkSync(join(REPO_ROOT, 'node_modules/vite'), join(root, 'node_modules/vite'));
    41+ writeFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), '{"name":"scratch","type":"module"}');
    42+ for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(envFiles)) writeFileSync(join(root, name), text);
    43+ return root;
    44+}
    45+
    46+afterEach(() => {
    47+ vi.unstubAllEnvs();
    48+ vi.restoreAllMocks();
    49+ for (const dir of scratch.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    50+});
    51+
    52+describe('cairnManifest config hook, __CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__', () => {
    53+ it('is true while Vite serves', async () => {
    54+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', undefined);
    55+ expect(await defineFor('serve', 'development')).toBe('true');
    56+ });
    57+
    58+ it('is false in a default build', async () => {
    59+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', undefined);
    60+ vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(appRootWith({}));
    61+ expect(await defineFor('build', 'production')).toBe('false');
    62+ });
    63+
    64+ it('is true in a build when VITE_CAIRN_E2E=1 is in the process env', async () => {
    65+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', '1');
    66+ vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(appRootWith({}));
    67+ expect(await defineFor('build', 'production')).toBe('true');
    68+ });
    69+
    70+ it('is true in a build when only a .env.production file sets the flag', async () => {
    71+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', undefined);
    72+ vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(appRootWith({ '.env.production': 'VITE_CAIRN_E2E=1\n' }));
    73+ expect(await defineFor('build', 'production')).toBe('true');
    74+ });
    75+
    76+ it.each(['0', '', 'true'])('is false in a build when VITE_CAIRN_E2E is %j', async (value) => {
    77+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', value);
    78+ vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(appRootWith({}));
    79+ expect(await defineFor('build', 'production')).toBe('false');
    80+ });
    81+
    82+ it('leaves a define the config already carries alone', async () => {
    83+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', '1');
    84+ vi.spyOn(process, 'cwd').mockReturnValue(appRootWith({}));
    85+ expect(await defineFor('build', 'production', { define: { __CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__: 'false' } })).toBeUndefined();
    86+ });
    87+});
    88+
    89+describe('cairnManifest config hook, plugin order', () => {
    90+ const sitePlugin: Plugin = {
    91+ name: 'site-dev-build-define',
    92+ config: () => ({ define: { __CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__: 'false' } }),
    93+ };
    94+
    95+ /** The define a resolved build config carries, with the plugins in the given order. */
    96+ async function resolvedDefine(plugins: Plugin[]) {
    97+ vi.stubEnv('VITE_CAIRN_E2E', '1');
    98+ const resolved = await resolveConfig(
    99+ { configFile: false, root: REPO_ROOT, logLevel: 'silent', plugins },
    100+ 'build',
    101+ );
    102+ return resolved.define?.__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__;
    103+ }
    104+
    105+ it('keeps a site-set false when the engine plugin runs first', async () => {
    106+ expect(await resolvedDefine([cairnManifest(OPTS), sitePlugin])).toBe('false');
    107+ });
    108+
    109+ it('keeps a site-set false when the engine plugin runs second', async () => {
    110+ expect(await resolvedDefine([sitePlugin, cairnManifest(OPTS)])).toBe('false');
    111+ });
    112+
    113+ it('supplies the define when the site sets none', async () => {
    114+ expect(await resolvedDefine([cairnManifest(OPTS)])).toBe('true');
    115+ });
    116+});

    274+```svelte
    275+<!-- @component The custom Signups admin screen: a developer's own route rendered in CairnAdminShell.
    276+ The header and the table adopt the packaged admin toolkit through its public subpath
    277+ (`@glw907/cairn-cms/admin-toolkit`), the in-repo consumer proof that a site's own custom
    278+ screen reaches for the toolkit the same way cairn's own admin does. -->
    279+<script lang="ts">
    280+ import { tick } from 'svelte';
    281+ import { enhance } from '$app/forms';
    282+ import { CsrfField } from '@glw907/cairn-cms/admin';
    283+ import { PageHeader, AdminTable } from '@glw907/cairn-cms/admin-toolkit';
    284+ import type { PageData, ActionData } from './$types';
    285+ import type { SubmitFunction } from '$app/forms';
    286+
    287+ let { data, form }: { data: PageData; form: ActionData } = $props();
    288+
    289+ // The server's error tokens stay terse (other tests and the exemplar's docs name them), so the
    290+ // sentence a sighted user reads is built here, with the raw token as a fallback for any token
    291+ // this map does not yet cover.
    292+ const errorMessages: Record<string, string> = {
    293+ missing: 'Name and email are both required.',
    294+ };
    295+
    296+ // State for the one shared confirm dialog, whose markup and recipe sit below the table: the
    297+ // pending row's id and name are set by the trigger that opened it, so the same dialog and the
    298+ // same posted form serve every row without duplicating a dialog per row.
    299+ let deleteDialog = $state<HTMLDialogElement | null>(null);
    300+ let pendingDeleteId = $state<number | null>(null);
    301+ let pendingDeleteName = $state('');
    302+ let nameInput = $state<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
    303+
    304+ function confirmDelete(id: number, name: string) {
    305+ pendingDeleteId = id;
    306+ pendingDeleteName = name;
    307+ // showModal only after Svelte flushes the new pendingDeleteName, or the dialog's
    308+ // aria-labelledby heading still names the previously opened row (or nothing, on the first
    309+ // open): $state writes batch into a microtask, so a synchronous showModal races it.
    310+ void tick().then(() => deleteDialog?.showModal());
    311+ }
    312+
    313+ function cancelDelete() {
    314+ deleteDialog?.close();
    315+ }
    316+
    317+ // use:enhance is what keeps the outcome region's content change inside the live document: a
    318+ // native full-page POST would replace the whole document with the region's outcome already
    319+ // present at load, which a screen reader never announces as a status change (WCAG 4.1.3).
    320+ const onCreate: SubmitFunction = () => {
    321+ return async ({ result, update }) => {
    322+ await update();
    323+ if (result.type === 'failure') nameInput?.focus();
    324+ };
    325+ };
    326+
    327+ const onRemove: SubmitFunction = () => {
    328+ return async ({ result, update }) => {
    329+ if (result.type === 'success') deleteDialog?.close();
    330+ await update();
    331+ };
    332+ };
    333+</script>
    334+
    335+<PageHeader title="Signups" />
    336+
    337+<form method="POST" action="?/create" class="my-4 flex items-end gap-2" use:enhance={onCreate}>
    338+ <CsrfField />
    339+ <label class="flex flex-col gap-label signup-create-label">
    340+ <span class="type-body font-medium">Name</span>
    341+ <input
    342+ name="name"
    343+ class="input signup-create-field"
    344+ bind:this={nameInput}
    345+ aria-describedby="signup-outcome"
    346+ aria-invalid={form?.error ? 'true' : undefined}
    347+ />
    348+ </label>
    349+ <label class="flex flex-col gap-label signup-create-label">
    350+ <span class="type-body font-medium">Email</span>
    351+ <input
    352+ name="email"
    353+ class="input signup-create-field"
    354+ aria-describedby="signup-outcome"
    355+ aria-invalid={form?.error ? 'true' : undefined}
    356+ />
    357+ </label>
    358+ <button class="btn btn-primary signup-create-submit">Add</button>
    359+</form>
    360+
    361+<!-- Always mounted and content-gated (the admin's ruled busy/live-region idiom), so it reads any
    362+ outcome either action produces without re-mounting mid-interaction (WCAG 4.1.3, 3.3.1): both
    363+ forms' use:enhance keeps the outcome a DOM mutation into this already-mounted region rather
    364+ than a full-page reload. form.error is read generically: createSectionAction's own denial and
    365+ misconfigured branches carry the same field the create action's validation failure does. -->
    366+<p role="status" aria-live="polite" class="type-body mt-2 scroll-mt-14" id="signup-outcome">
    367+ {#if form?.error}
    368+ {errorMessages[form.error] ?? form.error}
    369+ {:else if form?.created}
    370+ Signup added.
    371+ {:else if form?.removed}
    372+ Signup removed.
    373+ {/if}
    374+</p>
    375+
    376+<AdminTable density="sm" rowCount={data.signups.length}>
    377+ {#snippet header()}
    378+ <th scope="col">Name</th>
    379+ <th scope="col">Email</th>
    380+ <th scope="col"><span class="sr-only">Actions</span></th>
    381+ {/snippet}
    382+ {#snippet children()}
    383+ {#each data.signups as s (s.id)}
    384+ <tr>
    385+ <td>{s.name}</td>
    386+ <td>{s.email}</td>
    387+ <td>
    388+ <button
    389+ type="button"
    390+ class="btn btn-ghost btn-xs"
    391+ aria-label={`Delete ${s.name}`}
    392+ aria-haspopup="dialog"
    393+ onclick={() => confirmDelete(s.id, s.name)}
    394+ >
    395+ Delete
    396+ </button>
    397+ </td>
    398+ </tr>
    399+ {/each}
    400+ {/snippet}
    401+</AdminTable>
    402+
    403+<!-- One shared confirm for every row's destructive action, following the design system's
    404+ safe-delete recipe: a native dialog opened with showModal (native focus trap and Escape),
    405+ role="alertdialog", and no method="dialog" backdrop, so a stray click cannot dismiss it. -->
    406+<dialog
    407+ class="modal"
    408+ role="alertdialog"
    409+ aria-modal="true"
    410+ aria-labelledby="signup-delete-title"
    411+ bind:this={deleteDialog}
    412+>
    413+ <div class="modal-box">
    414+ <h2 id="signup-delete-title" class="type-heading font-bold">
    415+ Delete {pendingDeleteName}?
    416+ </h2>
    417+ <p class="mb-3 type-body">This cannot be undone.</p>
    418+ <form method="POST" action="?/remove" class="flex justify-end gap-2" use:enhance={onRemove}>
    419+ <CsrfField />
    420+ <input type="hidden" name="id" value={pendingDeleteId} />
    421+ <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" onclick={cancelDelete}>Cancel</button>
    422+ <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-error">Delete</button>
    423+ </form>
    424+ </div>

    427+<style>
    428+ /* The site admin sheet scans this route (`@source "./routes/admin"` in src/admin.css), so a
    429+ Tailwind utility would resolve here; the field width the stacked labels need is a scoped rule
    430+ because the flex, min and max sizing below reads better as one named block than as a
    431+ utility stack.
    432+
    433+ The label, not the input, carries the sizing: as a flex item with a definite flex-basis it
    434+ grows to 20rem when the row has room and shrinks below that (down to 3rem) when it does not,
    435+ so the create row never overflows or wraps at narrow viewports. The input then fills its
    436+ label at 100%, which resolves cleanly here because the label (unlike `.input`'s own auto-sized
    437+ flex-col containing block) now has a definite computed width from the flex algorithm. */
    438+ .signup-create-label {

    440+ min-width: 3rem;
    441+ max-width: 20rem;
    442+ }

    444+ .signup-create-field {

    453+
    454+Its `+page.server.ts`, which reads and writes the developer's own `signups` table through a D1
    455+binding the site declares itself. The access rule it relies on lives in the showcase adapter's
    456+`access` member; a site that copies the screen adds its own rule for the route.
    457+
    458+```ts
    459+// Archetype: the custom admin screen over the site's own table.
    460+// Atoms: requireAccess, createSectionAction, createLogger.
    461+// Recipe: docs/extend/add-a-custom-admin-screen.md.
    462+//
    463+// A developer's own custom admin screen, proving the extension seam. It is a concrete route
    464+// under /admin (so it wins over the catch-all), inherits the guard-populated locals.cairnEditor, renders
    465+// inside the shared CairnAdminShell from the parent layout, and reads and writes its own APP_DB
    466+// binding (the engine never touches it). requireAccess on the load and the section action's own
    467+// access check on each form action resolve against the same site access map, so a denied POST's
    468+// page render exposes nothing the load would already have refused; the ownerOnly nav flag is
    469+// cosmetic only.
    470+import type { PageServerLoad, Actions } from './$types';
    471+import { env } from 'cloudflare:workers';
    472+import { createSectionAction, requireAccess } from '@glw907/cairn-cms/sveltekit';
    473+import { error, fail } from '@sveltejs/kit';
    474+import type { D1Database } from '@cloudflare/workers-types';
    475+import { log } from '#lib/log.js';
    476+
    477+/** A signup row, the developer's own table shape, read from APP_DB. */
    478+interface SignupRow {
    479+ id: number;
    480+ name: string;
    481+ email: string;
    482+}
    483+
    484+// A deployed Worker always carries APP_DB (wrangler.jsonc binds it); its absence is a
    485+// deployment misconfiguration, not a request-shaped failure, so it logs with the engine's own
    486+// area.subject.verb_phrase grammar (section-action.ts's admin.action.misconfigured) and fails
    487+// closed with a generic 500 rather than leaking binding detail to the client. The load resolves
    488+// the binding this way because createSectionAction wraps form actions only; requireAccess and
    489+// requireOwner are the documented gates for a load.
    490+function requireAppDb(): D1Database {
    491+ const db: D1Database | undefined = env.APP_DB;
    492+ if (!db) {
    493+ log.error('admin.signups.misconfigured', { reason: 'db_not_bound' });
    494+ error(500, 'This screen is not configured.');
    495+ }
    496+ return db;
    497+}
    498+
    499+export const load: PageServerLoad = async (event) => {
    500+ requireAccess(event);
    501+ const db = requireAppDb();
    502+ const { results } = await db
    503+ .prepare('SELECT id, name, email FROM signups ORDER BY id DESC')
    504+ .all<SignupRow>();
    505+ return { signups: results };
    506+};
    507+
    508+// This screen's job is to teach the documented path, so it copies the wrapper rather than the
    509+// minimum that compiles: createSectionAction (@glw907/cairn-cms/sveltekit) is what a site's own
    510+// admin section reaches for, and a developer copying this route should carry it across. It
    511+// composes the editor, CSRF and audit contract onto every action and resolves the section's own
    512+// binding, so no action re-implements a gate the engine already owns.
    513+//
    514+// It is fail-closed on every call, unlike createAdminAction's opt-in access option: the site's access
    515+// declaration (the adapter's `access` member in src/theme/cairn.config.ts) must carry a rule
    516+// admitting the session for this route, or the action refuses with a 403 it never explains to the
    517+// browser, and a route no hook attached the map to refuses with a 500. ownerOnly stacks on top of that map check for the destructive
    518+// action, never in place of it.
    519+const sectionAction = createSectionAction<Env, D1Database>({
    520+ resolveDb: (workerEnv: Env | undefined) => workerEnv?.APP_DB,
    521+});
    522+
    523+export const actions: Actions = {
    524+ create: sectionAction(
    525+ async ({ form, ctx }) => {
    526+ const name = String(form.get('name') ?? '').trim();
    527+ const email = String(form.get('email') ?? '').trim();
    528+ // A rejected request mutated nothing, so it owes no audit record.
    529+ if (!name || !email) return fail(400, { error: 'missing' });
    530+ await ctx.db
    531+ .prepare('INSERT INTO signups (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)')
    532+ .bind(name, email)
    533+ .run();
    534+ ctx.audit({ detail: email });
    535+ return { created: true };
    536+ },
    537+ { action: 'create', entity: 'signup' },
    538+ ),
    539+ remove: sectionAction(
    540+ async ({ form, ctx }) => {
    541+ const id = Number(form.get('id'));
    542+ await ctx.db.prepare('DELETE FROM signups WHERE id = ?').bind(id).run();
    543+ ctx.audit({ entityId: id });
    544+ return { removed: true };
    545+ },
    546+ // The destructive action keeps the owner gate the map check alone would not supply: every
    547+ // role the map admits may add a signup, only an owner may remove one.
    548+ { action: 'remove', entity: 'signup', ownerOnly: true },
    549+ ),
    550+};
    551+```

    1+// The pure half of the feed: maps a site's posts into cairn-cms/delivery's FeedItem shape from
    2+// injected pieces, so a unit test drives it without the theme's Svelte imports. feed.ts binds it
    3+// to this site.
    4+import type { CairnAdapter } from '@glw907/cairn-cms';
    5+import {
    6+ createFragmentResolver,
    7+ createLinkResolver,
    8+ type FeedItem,
    9+ type MediaResolve,
    10+ type SiteResolver,
    11+} from '@glw907/cairn-cms/delivery';
    12+
    13+/** What the feed reads: the site, its origin, the render call, and the media resolver. */
    14+export interface FeedSource {
    15+ site: SiteResolver;
    16+ origin: string;
    17+ render: CairnAdapter['rendering']['render'];
    18+ resolveMedia: MediaResolve;
    19+}
    20+
    21+/**
    22+ * Map a site's posts into feed items. A feed body leaves the site, so each link and each image
    23+ * URL is absolute, and `::include` fragments render from the site's own fragments.
    24+ */
    25+export async function feedItemsFrom({
    26+ site,
    27+ origin,
    28+ render,
    29+ resolveMedia,
    30+}: FeedSource): Promise<FeedItem[]> {
    31+ const posts = site.concept('posts');
    32+ if (!posts) return [];
    33+ const toPermalink = createLinkResolver(site);
    34+ const resolve = (ref: Parameters<typeof toPermalink>[0]) => origin + toPermalink(ref);
    35+ const resolveFragment = createFragmentResolver(site);
    36+ const resolveAbsoluteMedia: MediaResolve = (ref) => {
    37+ const url = resolveMedia(ref);
    38+ return url === undefined ? undefined : new URL(url, origin).href;
    39+ };
    40+ return Promise.all(
    41+ posts.all().map(async (p) => ({
    42+ title: p.title,
    43+ url: origin + p.permalink,
    44+ date: p.date,
    45+ summary: p.excerpt,
    46+ contentHtml: await render({
    47+ body: posts.byId(p.id)!.body,
    48+ resolve,
    49+ resolveMedia: resolveAbsoluteMedia,
    50+ resolveFragment,
    51+ }),
    52+ tags: p.tags,
    53+ })),
    54+ );
    55+}

    1+<!--
    2+@component
    3+The admin's error page: a failure in any /admin/** page renders inside the shell and its theme
    4+wrapper, so a refusal or an unknown address reads as the admin's own page, not the public site's.
    5+A 403 and a 404 carry their own calm copy; any other status falls back to the thrown message.
    6+
    7+SvelteKit renders a route's `+error.svelte` inside the layouts above it, which is why the shell
    8+frames this page. A failure in the admin layout's own load has no layout above it to render
    9+inside, so it falls to the root error page. SvelteKit requires that, and this file cannot change it.
    10+-->
    11+<script lang="ts">
    12+ import { page } from '$app/state';
    13+ import { EmptyState } from '@glw907/cairn-cms/admin-toolkit';
    14+
    15+ const copy = $derived(
    16+ page.status === 403
    17+ ? {
    18+ heading: "You don't have access to this page.",
    19+ message: "Your role doesn't include this page. Ask the site owner if you need access.",
    20+ }
    21+ : page.status === 404
    22+ ? {
    23+ heading: "This page doesn't exist.",
    24+ message: 'Check the address, or go back to the dashboard.',
    25+ }
    26+ : {
    27+ heading: 'Something went wrong.',
    28+ message: page.error?.message ?? 'Try again, or go back to the dashboard.',
    29+ },
    30+ );
    31+</script>
    32+
    33+<EmptyState heading={copy.heading} headingLevel="h1" message={copy.message}>
    34+ {#snippet action()}
    35+ <a href="/admin" class="btn btn-neutral btn-sm">Back to the dashboard</a>
    36+ {/snippet}
    37+</EmptyState>
